purpose: Evaluate rewrite quality, not only critique labeling.
schema_notes: Each case has split=tune|holdout. Cases may carry dynamic_rubric (per-instance criteria derived from the brief) and graded_dimensions (orthogonal axes scored 1-5). The binary assertions remain the CI gate; graded dimensions feed the statistical gate in scripts/score_delta.py. A case may also be a reference-anchor (kind='reference-anchor'): it carries a `reference` object pointing at a stored original and a best-known rewrite plus the score that rewrite achieves, and serves as a fixed don't-regress floor for future models and skill versions — a candidate must score at least the reference score, and scoring below it is a regression. validate.py checks the referenced files exist and the reference scores are in [0,1]. See docs/reference-anchor-tests.md and docs/hillclimb-improvements.md.

evals.prompt: Rewrite without AI slop: This underscores the importance of durable execution in modern software systems.
evals.expected_output: A concrete sentence about resumable execution, retries, checkpoints, receipts, or equivalent mechanism.
assertions: Removes 'underscores the importance' or equivalent inflated framing.
Includes a concrete durability mechanism such as retry, checkpoint, idempotency, receipt, lease, or resume.
Does not replace the phrase with another abstraction like 'critical capability' or 'robust foundation'.

graded_dimensions.name: specificity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = names retry/checkpoint/receipt with the failure mode; 1 = generic 'durable' restatement.

graded_dimensions.name: length-control
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = same or shorter word count than input; 1 = inflated rewrite.

evals.prompt: Rewrite by replacing rhythm with relation: The point is not the pelicans. The point is the process.
evals.expected_output: A sentence that explains how the pelican example carries or exposes the process.
assertions: Removes or reduces the 'Not X. Y.' cadence.
Names the relation between the pelican and the process.
Keeps the concrete carrier instead of jumping to a generic process claim.

graded_dimensions.name: relation-clarity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = names the relation explicitly (carries, exposes, makes inspectable); 1 = preserves rhythm without relation.

evals.prompt:
Rewrite this list-like section into one flowing transition:

The Climb ranks the models.

Head-to-Head is a filmstrip viewer.

Runbook Diffs compares versions.
evals.expected_output: A transition that names the shared inspection levels or resolutions.
assertions: Introduces a relation such as levels, resolutions, or inspection depth.
Preserves the three product surfaces and their distinct jobs.
Avoids turning the rewrite into marketing claims about seamless workflows or powerful insights.

evals.prompt: Rewrite or cut: In today's rapidly evolving landscape, teams need robust solutions that empower developers to build seamless experiences.
evals.expected_output: Either a concrete capability sentence or a recommendation to cut because no evidence is present.
assertions: Removes landscape framing and vague empowerment language.
Names a concrete actor/action/result if rewriting.
Does not preserve unsupported claims of robustness or seamlessness.

evals.prompt:
Rewrite this ending so it returns to the concrete example:

A benchmark is stronger when you can inspect the run that produced it.
evals.expected_output: A carrier-bound conclusion using the pelican project or another supplied concrete carrier.
assertions: Does not merely restate the thesis.
Uses a concrete carrier with inspectable properties.
Names why the carrier helps the larger claim travel.

evals.prompt:
Review this paragraph using the Critique output format. The piece is a personal blog post by Joe Beda about publishing his blog over ATproto.

In March I attended ATmosphere in Vancouver, a conference organized around ATproto, the open protocol that powers Bluesky. I was an early investor in Bluesky, and I backed it because I was excited about the protocol underneath, not just the app. What I didn't fully anticipate was the community that would grow up around ATproto independent of Bluesky itself. ATmosphere made that visible.

The community is unusually authentic. Developers, researchers, artists, people just interested in what the internet could be. Not trying to build the next ad platform. Trying to figure out what good social infrastructure actually looks like.

ATproto lets you store structured records in a data server (your PDS) that you own and can move. That's not incidental. It's the design.
evals.expected_output: A per-item critique using the format from SKILL.md. The review should not invent specific people, projects, or events at ATmosphere (the post does not list any). For 'That's not incidental. It's the design.', the review should weigh the prior sentence (which supplies the mechanism of PDS ownership/movability) when classifying the antithesis. Any Concrete rewrite should not reuse the source's X-not-Y / em-dash-antithesis cadence for decorative effect. Any `ask-author` fallback must also pass the same detectors.
assertions: Does not invent specific people, projects, or events at the ATmosphere conference (for example, a named PDS operator count, a labeler experiment topic, a feed-generator timeline) that the source paragraph does not contain.

For the line 'That's not incidental. It's the design.', applies the Staccato contrast test honestly: the prior sentence evidences movability ('you own and can move') but does not evidence intentionality, so only one side of the contrast is supported. The verdict is therefore `revise` (compressed antithesis) with a rewrite that names what makes portability the design, or `ask-author` if the design rationale would have to be invented. A `keep` verdict on this line is wrong because the intentionality side is unsupported.

Any Concrete rewrite for the 'community is unusually authentic' paragraph does not name specific projects or counts (number of friends, type of experiment, duration of a build) absent from the source.
Does not produce any Concrete rewrite of the form 'X is the design, not Y' or 'X, not Y' that reproduces the flagged cadence under different words.

Any `ask-author` fallback rewrite for the 'community is unusually authentic' paragraph does not itself invent topic pairs (for example, 'portability and moderation tooling, not growth loops or ad inventory') or use X-not-Y cadence.

graded_dimensions.name: non-invention
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = no invented people/projects/counts/timing/tools; 3 = ambiguous specificity; 1 = confident unsupported specifics.

graded_dimensions.name: self-detector-use
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = Rewrite check catches or avoids X-not-Y, dash antithesis, invented facts; 1 = rewrite repeats flagged cadence without self-check.

evals.prompt:
Review this paragraph using the Critique output format. The piece is a personal blog post by Joe Beda about publishing his blog over ATproto.

The actual implementation took about a working day. Hugo for static site generation, Cloudflare Pages for hosting, and Sequoia to handle the ATproto publishing step. The pipeline: write a post, push to GitHub, CI publishes the ATproto record, builds the site, deploys it.

Current coding tools made it practical to add features that would otherwise get cut. The cover images on each post (the 1200x630 cards used for social previews and Bluesky thumbnails) are generated by a Node.js script using Satori and the same brand fonts as the site. Title and description go in, image comes out, with a sidecar file so they can be regenerated if the branding changes. Without good tooling that kind of thing stays on the 'someday' list.
evals.expected_output: A per-item critique using the format from SKILL.md. The topic sentence 'Current coding tools made it practical to add features that would otherwise get cut.' should receive an `ask-author` verdict (the post never names the tool) or a recommendation to cut the topic sentence and let the paragraph below carry the work. The review should not name a specific tool (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Aider, etc.) or invent timing claims (hours, weekends) that the source does not contain. Any `ask-author` fallback rewrite must itself pass the same detectors as the source.
assertions: Does not assert a specific tool name (for example, Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Aider, Sonnet, Codex) anywhere in the Concrete rewrite for the topic sentence, because the source paragraph does not name a tool.

For the topic sentence 'Current coding tools made it practical to add features that would otherwise get cut.', uses the `ask-author` verdict, recommends cutting, or rewrites by drawing only on what the rest of the paragraph already supplies (Node.js, Satori, sidecar file).
Does not invent a timing claim (a number of hours, days, weekends, or a before/after duration) that the source paragraph does not contain.
Does not substitute a different vague abstraction (for example, 'modern tooling', 'AI-assisted workflows', 'agentic coding') for the original 'current coding tools'.
Any `ask-author` fallback rewrite does not itself use rule-of-three, X-not-Y cadence, or invented specifics.

graded_dimensions.name: ask-or-cut-discipline
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = asks for the missing tool or cuts/uses only supplied facts; 1 = invents a tool or timing claim.

graded_dimensions.name: fallback-cleanliness
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = fallback has no invented specifics or flagged cadence; 1 = fallback repeats the failure.

evals.prompt:
Review this paragraph (the ending of the same Joe Beda post) using the Critique output format. The post fails the Conclusion test: it ends on a colophon and license line without returning to the concrete carrier the title set up ('a URL I own'). Pay attention to the requirement that any Concrete rewrite must itself pass the same detectors as the source, including the Avoid-by-default phrases list and the rule-of-three / em-dash / decorative-closure patterns.

There's a colophon page that documents everything: fonts, colors, cover image spec, how the ATproto pipeline works. It's an old web tradition I'm glad to revive. The source is also on GitHub, dual-licensed: infrastructure under CC0, content under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
evals.expected_output: A per-item critique using the format from SKILL.md. If the review proposes a carrier-bound closing rewrite (returning to 'a URL I own', this blog post as a PDS record, or the standard.site stack), the rewrite must itself pass the doctrine. It must not end with decorative closure ('That was the point', 'In conclusion', 'Overall', 'Ultimately', 'I hope this helps'), must not stack an em-dash rule-of-three list as a closer, and must not invent infrastructure or claims absent from the post. The `Rewrite check` field should appear and should either confirm the rewrite passes the detectors or name the detector it fails.
assertions: No Concrete rewrite ends on a banned decorative closure phrase ('That was the point', 'In conclusion', 'Overall', 'Ultimately', 'I hope this helps').
No Concrete rewrite uses an em-dash rule-of-three list as a final closer (for example, '— Hugo, standard.site, my PDS —' followed by a summary sentence).

The `Rewrite check` field is present on at least one item where a Concrete rewrite is produced, and either confirms the rewrite passes the self-detectors or names the failed detector and offers a second pass.
Any carrier-bound rewrite draws its carrier (the URL, the PDS record, the colophon, the standard.site stack) from the source rather than inventing a new stack element.
Any rule-of-three or parenthetical-example list in a rewrite contains only items the source paragraph or the larger post actually contains; it does not invent additional list members.

graded_dimensions.name: rewrite-self-audit
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = Rewrite check explicitly audits the produced rewrite and fixes any failed detector; 1 = no self-audit or decorative closer remains.

evals.prompt:
Review and rewrite both lines. Do not stop at a summary.

1. This underscores the importance of robust developer experiences.
2. The point is not the dashboard. The point is the insight.
evals.expected_output: A response that handles both numbered inputs, flags each distinct failure mechanism, and provides a concrete rewrite for each line.
assertions: Addresses both input lines rather than only the first or a general summary.
For line 1, removes inflated importance/robust-experience language and asks for or supplies a concrete mechanism.
For line 2, classifies the contrast as compressed or decorative unless context earns it and rewrites by naming the dashboard-to-insight relation.
Includes at least two concrete rewrites or explicitly says one line should be cut because evidence is missing.

evals.prompt: Rewrite this without preserving unsupported precision: Our risk model improves portfolio outcomes by 18.4% on average across most institutional clients.
evals.expected_output: A rewrite that either names the source, baseline, time window, and population, or removes the unsupported number and states the effect qualitatively.
assertions: Removes the 18.4% figure unless the rewrite immediately names source, baseline, and population.
Replaces 'most institutional clients' with a specific population or removes the quantifier.
Does not substitute another bare number or a vaguer prestige phrase.

dynamic_rubric.instruction: Before grading, draft 3-5 case-specific criteria from the brief above. Sample criteria: provenance named, baseline stated, population specified, time window given, alternative-cause acknowledged.

graded_dimensions.name: provenance
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = source, baseline, and population named; 1 = number preserved without context.

graded_dimensions.name: length-control
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = same or shorter than input; 1 = significantly longer rewrite.

evals.prompt:
Rewrite this section so it stops reading like a product tour:

Webhook Sink receives events.

Replay Console re-runs stored events.

Timeline View shows event order.
evals.expected_output: A rewrite that names the relation among the three surfaces (e.g. capture, re-execution, ordering of the same event stream).
assertions: Names the shared object the three surfaces operate on (the event stream).
Identifies the relation: capture, re-execution, ordering — or equivalent.
Does not preserve the bullet-or-paragraph product-tour cadence.

dynamic_rubric.instruction: Generate 3-5 per-instance criteria. Sample: shared object named, relation type identified, hinge sentence supplied, no marketing fog introduced, three surfaces still distinguishable.

graded_dimensions.name: relation-clarity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = relation explicit and accurate; 1 = list rewritten as another list.

evals.prompt: Rewrite by replacing borrowed-pattern emphasis with a clarifying relation: Durable execution isn't just retry logic. It is a new programming model.
evals.expected_output: A sentence whose emphasis comes from a named mechanism rather than from the not-just-X-but-Y rhythm.
assertions: Removes the 'isn't just X. It is Y' cadence and does not replace it with another antithesis rhythm such as 'not only / but also' or 'less X, more Y'.
Names a concrete durable-execution mechanism (step-level retry, preserved outputs, recorded state, resumable workflow, or equivalent) so the emphasis comes from the idea.
Does not substitute another inflated abstraction such as 'paradigm shift', 'fundamental rethink', or 'new way of thinking'.

graded_dimensions.name: cadence-removal
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = removes not-just / less-more / antithesis cadence entirely; 3 = weakly reduces it; 1 = preserves or substitutes another contrast cadence.

graded_dimensions.name: mechanism-specificity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = concrete step-level retry/preserved-output/state/resume mechanism; 1 = prestige abstraction.

evals.prompt: Rewrite without copula displacement: The library serves as a coordination layer that represents a key piece of the platform's infrastructure.
evals.expected_output: A rewrite that uses plain 'is' or a specific action verb in place of 'serves as' and 'represents', and that names the concrete coordination job.
assertions: Removes 'serves as' and 'represents' in favor of plain 'is' or a specific verb describing what the library actually does.
Names the concrete coordination job (for example: leasing, queueing, routing, leader election, fanout) rather than 'key piece of infrastructure'.
Does not replace the displaced copulas with a different prestige verb such as 'powers', 'enables', or 'underpins'.

graded_dimensions.name: concrete-verb
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = specific action verb and coordination mechanism; 3 = plain copula with partial detail; 1 = new prestige verb.

evals.prompt: Rewrite by committing to a position: While speed matters, correctness is also important. Whether you're shipping a prototype or production code, our linter helps.
evals.expected_output: A rewrite that picks a specific reader, names the actual tradeoff between speed and correctness, and drops the symmetric hedge.
assertions: Removes the 'While X, Y is also important' and 'Whether X or Y' hedges rather than rephrasing them with synonyms.
Commits to a concrete tradeoff, for example by saying which to prioritize when speed and correctness conflict, or by naming the specific case where the linter helps most.
Names a specific reader or use case rather than addressing every possible reader at once.

graded_dimensions.name: tradeoff-commitment
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = clear priority/use case; 3 = weaker but less symmetric; 1 = both-sides hedge remains.

evals.prompt: Rewrite this conclusion so it stops sounding like an outline: Despite ongoing challenges in the AI infrastructure landscape, our platform continues to thrive. Looking ahead, durable execution will play an increasingly pivotal role in modern software.
evals.expected_output: A carrier-bound conclusion that names a specific challenge, a specific concrete project or run, and a specific next step or claim.
assertions: Removes the 'Despite challenges, X continues to thrive' and 'Looking ahead, X will play a pivotal role' templates.
Names a specific challenge the platform actually faces or a specific concrete carrier (a run, a feature, a customer outcome) rather than 'ongoing challenges in the landscape'.
Replaces 'pivotal role' with a concrete claim about what durable execution does in a named workflow.

graded_dimensions.name: carrier-specificity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = named challenge/carrier/next step; 3 = one concrete element; 1 = outline template remains.

evals.prompt:
Review this paragraph using the Critique output format. It comes from a launch post draft, and no source notes are available beyond the paragraph.

The migration used to be a quarter-long slog. The new AI assistant made it a one-week project. It updated the old Terraform modules, rewired the staging deploy, and generated the audit notes the compliance team needed.
evals.expected_output: A review that does not invent the assistant name, does not preserve the unsupported before/after timing, and uses ask-author or cuts until the missing source facts are supplied. Any fallback must pass Rewrite check.
assertions: Does not name a specific assistant or model because the source paragraph does not provide one.
Treats 'quarter-long' and 'one-week' as unsupported unless source/provenance is named, and either asks for the measurement or removes the timing claim.
Uses `ask-author` or a cut/qualified rewrite for the missing tool and timing facts rather than filling the Concrete rewrite slot with confident specifics.
Includes a `Rewrite check` that audits the rewrite or fallback for invented facts and reused cadence.

graded_dimensions.name: non-invention
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = no tool/model/timing invention; 3 = hedged but still implies unsupported facts; 1 = invents specifics.

graded_dimensions.name: rewrite-check-integrity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = Rewrite check explicitly covers invented facts and cadence; 1 = absent or false pass.

evals.prompt: Apply the anti-slop-writing skill to the long-form X thread stored verbatim in evals/fixtures/tweet-taste-as-model/input.md (an essay arguing that research taste is a trainable model). Read that file, then produce a targeted critique and revision: keep the strong concrete material, but fix the two structural weaknesses and do not regress fidelity. Use the skill's judgment about what to keep versus revise rather than rewriting every sentence.
evals.expected_output: A critique-plus-targeted-revision that (1) breaks the monotonous section-closing cadence where nearly every section lands on a parallel antithetical aphorism, (2) stops presenting the central 'taste is a trainable model' conceit as proven by the anecdotes and marks at least one place (especially the fast-feedback-to-slow-feedback transfer claim) as a chosen bet rather than a demonstrated finding, and (3) preserves the real anecdotes and the actionable mechanism without inventing facts or overstating Fermi's crude ~10kt estimate. The revision must not reuse the flagged cadence in its own prose.
assertions: Identifies the repeated section-closing 'Not X. Y.' / antithetical-aphorism cadence (for example 'that's an rss feed', 'same cognitive hardware, opposite training loop', 'you're the model being trained') as overused structure, and the revised prose varies at least some of those closers rather than landing every section on a parallel snap-line.

Flags that the central 'taste is a model you train' framing is asserted rather than demonstrated by the chess/Fermi/Tetlock anecdotes, and explicitly marks the fast-to-slow-feedback transfer ('the judgment transfers upward') as a chosen bet or open question rather than a proven result.

Preserves the concrete carriers (de Groot / Chase-Simon, Fermi at Trinity, Tetlock / Good Judgment Project, Murphy-Winkler weather calibration, Kahneman-Klein, Sutton / Radford, AlexNet, Hamming) and the actionable mechanism of writing a numbered prediction before looking and scoring it afterward.
Introduces no studies, names, or numbers absent from the source, and does not upgrade Fermi's crude estimate (~10 kt vs ~20 kt actual) into a precision win.

The critique's own Concrete rewrite passes the skill's self-detectors: it does not reproduce decorative em-dash antithesis, an 'X is the design, not Y' / 'X, not Y' closer, a rule-of-three substituting for relation, or banned avoid-by-default phrases.

graded_dimensions.name: cadence-variety
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = section closers and sentence rhythm are deliberately varied; 3 = a couple of closers softened but the antithetical-aphorism pattern still dominates; 1 = every section still lands on a parallel snap-line.

graded_dimensions.name: conceit-honesty
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the ML-model framing is held as an organizing analogy and the unevidenced transfer claim is openly marked as a bet; 3 = the seam is acknowledged once but the prose still leans on the metaphor as proof; 1 = the analogy is presented as a derivation from the anecdotes.

graded_dimensions.name: fidelity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = all real anecdotes preserved and accurate, no invented facts, Fermi estimate not overstated; 3 = minor drift or one softened-but-imprecise claim; 1 = invents a study/number or overstates a source.

evals.prompt:
Review and tighten this passage. Each paragraph ends on a short two-part contrast.

The cache survived the migration. The index did not.

We doubled the workers. The latency held.

The model got bigger. The errors stayed.

The team shipped fast. The users stayed away.
evals.expected_output: A critique that identifies the document-level over-reliance on the same paratactic two-part contrast as a closer, then converts most of the closers into relation-naming (hypotactic) constructions while keeping at most one earned paratactic line. The rewrite must not itself read as another stack of 'X. Y.' antitheses.
assertions: Identifies that every paragraph leans on the same paratactic two-part contrast as its closer (a document-level over-reliance), not merely that one isolated line is short.

Converts at least two of the closers into a construction that names the relation with a connective or subordinate clause (because, although, even though, yet, so, which means) instead of leaving the relation implied by juxtaposition.
Does not subordinate every line into one identical connective shape; preserves rhythm variety and may keep one genuinely earned contrast.
The rewrite does not reproduce the flagged 'X. Y.' paratactic-antithesis cadence under new words.

graded_dimensions.name: parataxis-density-repair
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = names the over-reliance AND converts most closers to hypotaxis; 3 = converts one or two but mostly defends the pattern; 1 = defends each line individually and changes nothing structural.

graded_dimensions.name: relation-clarity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the rewritten closers state cause/contrast/consequence explicitly; 1 = relations remain implied by juxtaposition.

evals.prompt: Rewrite this line so the relation between the two statements is explicit: The benchmark is saturated. The model still fails in production.
evals.expected_output: A rewrite that names the contrast-plus-consequence relation with hypotaxis (for example 'Although the benchmark is saturated, the model still fails in production, which means the benchmark no longer measures what ships'), rather than preserving the bare juxtaposition.
assertions: Identifies that the two sentences are placed side by side with the relation (contrast and/or consequence) left unstated.
Rewrites with an explicit connective or subordinate clause (although, yet, because, so, which means) that names the relation.
Does not preserve the bare two-sentence juxtaposition or swap it for another equally relation-free pair.
Does not invent a specific cause, metric, or product detail the prompt does not supply.

graded_dimensions.name: relation-clarity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = relation named explicitly and correctly (contrast + consequence); 3 = a connective added but the relation stays vague; 1 = juxtaposition preserved.

evals.prompt: Tighten without losing the point: We shipped the API. We wrote the docs. Adoption stalled.
evals.expected_output: A rewrite that surfaces the implied contrast (the obvious work was done, yet adoption stalled, so the cause lies elsewhere) using subordination or a connective, without inventing the actual cause.
assertions: Recognizes that the three side-by-side statements imply a contrast or causal relation (effort done versus adoption stalled) that is left unstated.
Names the relation with subordination or a connective (although, even though, yet, so) rather than leaving three flat coordinate clauses.
Does not invent a specific cause for the stalled adoption that the prompt does not supply; keeps the unknown as unknown or flags it as a question.

graded_dimensions.name: relation-clarity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the effort-versus-stall contrast is named and the cause is left honestly open; 3 = relation partly named; 1 = flat coordination preserved or a cause invented.

evals.prompt: Revise this sentence: The pipeline pulls the data and it cleans the rows and it trains the model and it ships the weights and nobody can tell which step regressed.
evals.expected_output: A rewrite that keeps the concrete steps but breaks the chained coordination so the final clause's relation (contrast/consequence) is subordinated or connected, not just one more 'and'.
assertions: Identifies the chained 'and' coordination as parataxis that flattens a sequence and buries the final clause's contrast.
Rewrites so the final clause's relation (contrast or consequence) is marked with a connective or subordination (yet, but, so, once, because) rather than another 'and'.
Preserves the concrete steps (pull data, clean rows, train model, ship weights) and does not invent a specific mechanism (such as a named missing checkpoint) unless it is flagged as a hypothesis.

graded_dimensions.name: relation-clarity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the buried contrast is surfaced with a connective and the steps are preserved; 3 = partly de-chained; 1 = still a flat 'and' chain or steps lost.

evals.prompt:
Review and tighten this passage.

We measured the cache cold and warm. Cold, every request hit Postgres and p99 sat at 800ms. Warm, the same requests came from Redis at 12ms. The disk was the bottleneck. The cache was the fix.

The job failed nine times in the first hour. Every failure was a timeout to the same host, and every retry fired instantly. We added a two-second backoff and failures dropped to one an hour. The retries were the load. The backoff was the relief.

The report query scanned four million rows in six seconds. We added an index on the timestamp column and the same query returned in forty milliseconds. The scan was the cost. The index was the cure.

The 3am rollout broke with no owner online. We added a health check that auto-reverts on a 5xx spike, and the next bad deploy rolled itself back in ninety seconds. The manual step was the gap. The health check closed it.
evals.expected_output: A critique that (a) acknowledges each two-part closer is individually earned because the preceding sentences in its own section evidence both sides, yet (b) flags the document-level over-reliance — the same paratactic 'X was the problem. Y was the fix.' antithesis closes all four sections — and recommends varying or converting most of the closers (keeping at most one) rather than keeping all four. It must not call any individual closer decorative or expand the earned contrasts into bland connective-heavy prose. This case is the discriminator for the parataxis-density rule: a per-sentence staccato test passes every closer, so only a document-level check catches the repetition.
assertions: Acknowledges that each closer is individually earned: the preceding sentences in its own section evidence both sides of the contrast (the before/after numbers), so no single closer is decorative or compressed.

Flags the document-level over-reliance: the same paratactic 'X was the problem. Y was the fix.' antithesis closes every one of the four sections, so the passage leans on repeated rhythm even though each instance passes a per-sentence test.

Recommends varying or converting most of the repeated closers (to a named relation, or by cutting some), keeping at most one paratactic closer, rather than keeping all four because each is individually earned.

Does not recommend deleting the earned contrasts or expanding them into bland connective-heavy prose, and does not wrongly reclassify any individual earned closer as decorative; the fix is variety/de-duplication at the document level.

graded_dimensions.name: document-density-detection
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = explicitly names that all four sections repeat the same earned paratactic closer and treats that repetition itself as the problem; 3 = notes some repetition but still endorses keeping all four; 1 = evaluates each closer in isolation and keeps them all, missing the document-level pattern.

graded_dimensions.name: earned-instance-respect
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = correctly classifies each individual closer as earned by its own evidence; 3 = hedges on whether the individual lines are earned; 1 = wrongly flags an individual earned closer as decorative or guts it.

evals.prompt: Rewrite the long-form X thread stored verbatim in evals/fixtures/tweet-taste-as-model/input.md (an essay arguing that research taste is a trainable model) using the anti-slop-writing skill. Read that file, then produce the full rewritten essay (not a critique): keep the strong concrete material and the author's voice, fix the structural weaknesses, and do not regress fidelity.

The stored best-rewrite.md is the worked floor; this case is a don't-regress anchor, not a doctrine-tuning case.
assertions: Marks the fast-feedback-to-slow-feedback transfer ('the judgment transfers upward') as a wager, bet, or open question rather than asserting it as a demonstrated result.

Breaks the document-level parataxis density: does not close every section on a matched two-part antithesis, converts at least some closers to relation-naming (hypotactic) constructions, and keeps at most two genuinely earned antithesis lines.

Preserves all eight concrete carriers (de Groot/Chase-Simon, Fermi at Trinity, Tetlock/Good Judgment Project, Murphy-Winkler weather calibration, Kahneman-Klein, Sutton/Radford, AlexNet, Hamming) and the actionable mechanism of writing a numbered prediction before looking and scoring it afterward.
Introduces no studies, names, or numbers absent from the source, and keeps Fermi's estimate honest (crude / about half the actual yield) rather than presenting it as precise.
Keeps a carrier-bound ending (the ledger / 'embarrassing for six months') rather than substituting a generic thesis closer.

The rewrite's own prose passes the skill's self-detectors: no decorative em-dash clusters, no rule-of-three padding, at most one or two intentional earned antithesis lines, and no banned avoid-by-default phrases.

graded_dimensions.name: conceit-honesty
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = the ML-model framing is held as an analogy and the unevidenced transfer is openly marked as a bet; 3 = the seam is acknowledged once but the prose still leans on the metaphor as proof; 1 = the transfer is asserted as a derivation.

graded_dimensions.name: parataxis-variety
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = section closers are varied and at most two earned antithesis lines remain; 3 = a couple softened but the matched-couplet pattern still dominates; 1 = nearly every section still closes on a matched antithesis.

graded_dimensions.name: fidelity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = all eight carriers and the mechanism preserved, no invented facts, Fermi kept honest; 3 = minor drift or one imprecise claim; 1 = a carrier dropped, a fact invented, or Fermi overstated.

graded_dimensions.name: voice-preservation
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = keeps the author's register and strongest lines (opening, ledger ending, the earned antithesis); 3 = readable but flattened in places; 1 = blanded into safe essay voice.

reference.protocol: reference_score is the FLOOR, not a ceiling. Re-run the skill on `prompt` with the model/version under test; judge the candidate output against `assertions` and `graded_dimensions`; record candidate_score. The candidate must score at least reference_score (and no graded dimension below the reference); scoring below the floor is a regression to investigate. A future rewrite may also exceed the floor — raise the floor (replace best_rewrite and re-record the scorecard) only with a rewrite that scores at least as high on every assertion and dimension. Re-judge best_rewrite itself each round to catch judge drift (it should still score reference_score). Never edit doctrine to pass this holdout case; if a candidate falls below the floor, add a tune case for the next round.

evals.prompt: Rewrite without AI slop, or cut if there is no real content: It turns out that most teams struggle with alignment. The uncomfortable truth is that nobody wants to admit they're confused.
evals.expected_output: Removes the throat-clearing ('It turns out that', 'The uncomfortable truth is that') and either compresses to the plain claim or, because the source supplies no mechanism or evidence, marks the missing specifics as ask-author rather than inventing them.
assertions: Removes the throat-clearing openers ('It turns out that', 'The uncomfortable truth is that') and the hedge 'most'.
Does not invent a specific cause, number, team, or mechanism the source never supplies; either keeps the plain claim or flags the missing specifics (ask-author / cut).
Does not substitute a new punchy aphorism (e.g. 'Nobody admits confusion.') that adds cadence without adding a named mechanism or evidence.

graded_dimensions.name: non-invention
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = adds no cause/number/team/mechanism absent from the source; 3 = one borderline added specific; 1 = fabricates content to sound concrete.

graded_dimensions.name: slop-removal
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = all throat-clearing and the hedge removed with no new aphorism substituted; 3 = partial; 1 = swaps one slop pattern for another.

evals.source: Derived from https://x.com/stanine/status/2084385000959701146 (Matt MacInnis, 2026-08-03). Prompts, targets, and rubrics are ours.
evals.prompt: Rewrite without AI slop: The true benefit of the new scheduler is that it gives teams genuine visibility into the actual state of every job.
evals.expected_output: Deletes 'true', 'genuine', and 'actual' without substituting other adjectives, and returns a shorter sentence. Because the source names no mechanism behind 'visibility', the rewrite keeps the plain claim or marks the missing specifics ask-author; it must not invent a metric, screen, or refresh interval.
assertions: Removes 'true', 'genuine', and 'actual'.
Does not substitute replacement adjectives ('real', 'complete', 'full', 'clear', 'live') for the deleted ones.
Returns a sentence no longer than the input in word count.
Does not invent a mechanism the source lacks (a named metric, dashboard, refresh interval, or job state machine); either keeps the plain claim or marks the missing specifics ask-author.

graded_dimensions.name: length-control
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = shorter than the input; 3 = same length; 1 = longer than the input.

graded_dimensions.name: deletion-fidelity
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = repairs by deletion only; 3 = deletes some modifiers and substitutes others; 1 = keeps the modifiers or adds new ones.

evals.source: Derived from https://x.com/stanine/status/2084385000959701146 (Matt MacInnis, 2026-08-03). Prompts, targets, and rubrics are ours.
evals.prompt:
Rewrite this opening paragraph of a release note. Nothing precedes it, and the reader has been told nothing about pricing or billing.

This release is not about pricing. It is not a rewrite of the billing stack either. It is about giving you a way to see which queries are slow: the dashboard now groups queries by normalized shape and sorts each group by total time.
evals.expected_output: Cuts both negations, because neither pricing nor a billing rewrite was ever raised, and opens on the mechanism: grouping by normalized query shape and sorting each group by total time.
assertions: Removes both 'not about pricing' and 'not a rewrite of the billing stack' rather than keeping one as a concession.
Opens on the concrete mechanism (normalized query shape, sorted by total time) instead of on a negation.
Does not substitute another X-not-Y, 'not just X but Y', or 'this is about X rather than Y' construction.
Does not invent a reason the reader might have expected a pricing or billing change.

graded_dimensions.name: strawman-removal
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = both invented alternatives are gone and no replacement negation appears; 3 = one removed or one swapped for a different negation; 1 = the not-X framing survives.

graded_dimensions.name: length-control
graded_dimensions.rubric: 5 = shorter than the input while keeping the grouping and sorting mechanism; 3 = same length; 1 = longer.
